question: In asynchronous serial communication, what is the role of "Hardware Handshaking" (e.g., using RTS/CTS lines)?

options.text: To provide error detection using parity bits
To synchronize the internal clocks of both devices
To prevent data loss by managing buffer overflow

solution:
The correct answer is __**To prevent data loss by managing buffer overflow**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
 
 
• **Hardware Handshaking** refers to the use of control signals, such as **RTS (Request to Send) and CTS (Clear to Send)**, to coordinate data transmission between devices in **asynchronous serial communication**. 
 
• Its primary function is **to prevent data loss** by ensuring that the receiving device is ready to process incoming data before it is transmitted. 
 
• **RTS (Request to Send)** is a signal sent by the transmitting device to indicate that it is ready to send data, while **CTS (Clear to Send)** is a response from the receiving device indicating that it is ready to accept data. 
 
• By managing the flow of data, hardware handshaking helps avoid **buffer overflows**, which occur when a device receives more data than it can process or store.
